results.evidence: The North Side area page puts the wall base at 4,864 ft and the Pinto Rock location at 4,821 ft; the 5,118 ft figure is the formation's summit pin, which a 55 m route on the North Side does not reach. By catalog convention high_point_ft on crag routes tracks the base (4,864 ft here), but only one outside source gives that figure and no second source was found, so no patch. The 'topout' waypoint at 4,821 ft is really the pullout coordinate/area elevation, not a topout; same values are shared with Sidewinder and Top Gun.

The route page types Sidewinder as sport, bolts about every four feet to a chain anchor, and the North Side area listing agrees. patches.expect:
Route-finding complexity—alpine rock climbing with terrain variations; easy to wander off established line; study topo and photos
Loose and friable rock—typical Cascades granite; test holds and placements; helmet essential
Exposed scrambling on upper sections—significant consequences if climbing protection fails; runout potential between bolts
Weather exposure on open ridge—afternoon storms common; exposed position dangerous with lightning; start early
Descent route-finding—rappel and down-climbing required; terrain confusing in poor light; headlamp essential
Altitude exposure—7200+ feet; sustained climbing; altitude sickness possible; hydration management critical
Limited bailout options once committed to upper pitches—terrain becomes more serious as altitude increases; commit only in good conditions
Glacier/snow approach possible—seasonal variation; microspikes may be needed; assess conditions before approach
patches.value:
Rope running over the roof lip can rub and wear; extend the toprope so it runs clear of the edge
Lowering from Sidewinder's chains to the roof lip leaves the climber hanging in a steep, exposed spot to start
Steep, loose approach and exit trail below the North Side wall, especially with a pack
